title: Giving orders
description: Tell someone what to do, politely or not.

explanation.summary: Spanish has two ways to give an order. The tú form is the one you use with friends, and it is built from the yo form with the endings swapped. The usted form is polite, and it adds an r to the yo form.

sections.heading: Tú: swap the endings
sections.body: Take the yo form and give it the endings of tú: yo hablo, tú habla. Yo como, tú come. Yo escribo, tú escribe. There are eight verbs that break the rule: the eight irregular verbs in the present, which you already met. venir becomes ven, decir becomes di, and the three with a y change it to the opposite vowel: tengo becomes ten, venir becomes ven.

sections.heading: Usted: add an r
sections.body: The usted form adds an r to the yo form: yo hablo becomes hable, yo como becomes coma, yo escribo becomes escriba. It is polite, and it is what you use with anyone you should respect.

sections.heading: Saying no
sections.body: The negative command is no followed by the command: no hables, no vengas, no sea. And the command for usted is often softened with the word por favor, which is not required but never rude.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: For tú you use the opposite of the yo form: habla, come, escribe. For usted it adds an r: hable, coma, escriba.
